thread.title: African Markets - Factors to watch on Jan. 3 By Reuters

author: Reuters
title: African Markets - Factors to watch on Jan. 3 By Reuters
text:
© Reuters. African Markets - Factors to watch on Jan. 3 NAIROBI, Jan 3 (Reuters) - The following company announcements, scheduled economic indicators, debt and currency market moves and political events may affect African markets on Thursday.
- - - - - GLOBAL MARKETS U.S. stock futures fell on Thursday after a rare revenue warning from Apple Inc (NASDAQ: AAPL ) added to worries about slowing global growth, but a move by China's central bank to help struggling smaller firms lifted shares there, cushioning losses for Asian markets.
MKTS/GLOB WORLD OIL PRICES Oil prices fell on Thursday amid volatile currency and stock markets, and as analysts warned of an economic slowdown for 2019 just as crude supply is rising globally.
SOUTH AFRICA MARKETS South Africa's rand weakened more than one percent on Wednesday as weak Chinese manufacturing data offset hopes that a trade war between China and the United States was ending. KENYA CURRENCY The Kenyan shilling KES= was stable on Wednesday but players expected some weakening amid increased demand for hard currency from oil and goods importers as business activity resumed after the holiday, traders said.
NIGERIA CRUDE Total SA TOTF.PA said on Wednesday it had started production from the Egina oilfield off Nigeria's coast, part of a shift by the French energy firm towards deepwater oil and gas projects to its drive cashflow.
DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO ELECTIONS Results from Democratic Republic of Congo's chaotic presidential election could be delayed past Sunday's deadline because counting centres are still waiting for more than 80 percent of local tallies, the electoral commission said.
CURRENCY CRISIS Zimbabwe's largest brewing company Delta Corporation said on Wednesday that its beverages subsidiary will accept hard currency only from Jan. 4 to protect itself from a crippling shortage of U.S. dollars in the country.
